Welcomefrom the Headteacher
Welcome to Alder Grove Church of England Primary School
It is my great pleasure to welcome you to Alder Grove Church of England Primary School, where we continue to grow as a vibrant community of learning, grounded in our Christian Vision inspired by Psalm 1:3:
"They are like trees planted along the riverbank, bearing fruit each season."
As a school we aim for every child to flourish and thrive, nurtured by strong roots of personal development, knowledge, and character.
At Alder Grove, we believe that every child is uniquely created and deeply valued. Our dedicated staff work in partnership with families to provide an education that inspires curiosity, encourages creativity and builds confidence. Through a rich and engaging curriculum, we seek to develop children who are resilient, compassionate, and ready to make a positive difference in the world.
We are proud of our inclusive and nurturing environment, where Christian values are lived out daily and children are supported to achieve their very best, be that academically, socially and spiritually. Together, we grow strong, like the trees in our school vision, rooted in love and learning.
Whether you are a current member of our school family or exploring Alder Grove for the first time, we warmly invite you to discover more about our community and the joyful, purposeful learning that takes place here.

E-Safety
We understand that navigating the digital world can sometimes feel overwhelming, and we want to support you in helping your child develop healthy online habits. Below are some resources offering guidance on keeping children safe online:
UK Safer Internet Centre – Offers advice on online safety, privacy settings, and digital well-being: https://www.saferinternet.org.uk
NSPCC Online Safety – Practical guidance on managing risks and having open conversations about internet use: https://www.nspcc.org.uk/keeping-children-safe/online-safety/
Internet Matters – Age-specific advice, parental controls, and expert tips: https://www.internetmatters.org and guides to support you at home: Online safety leaflets & resources - Internet Matters
ThinkUKnow – Interactive resources designed to help parents and young people understand online risks: https://www.thinkuknow.co.uk
The Stay Safe Initiative - Initiative providing relevant, up to date education through engaging, workshops, assemblies, presentations and projects for young people or all ages, as well as programmes to support parents, school staff and people working closely with young people. The Stay Safe Initiative
Parenting in the Digital World - Parents Online Advice Sheet
At school, we regularly engage children in discussions and activities around online safety. We encourage you to continue these conversations at home
By working together - and while we are in the privileged position of guiding our children at a young age - we can help them develop positive lifelong digital habits. This will ensure they grow into safe, confident, and responsible digital citizens.

Our School Day
RECEPTION, KEY STAGE 1 & KEY STAGE 2
The school day starts at 8.45am am and finishes at 3.15pm. A rolling start will begin at 8.40am each morning and gates close at 8.45am.
10.40 – 10.55am (Key Stage 1&2)
Reception Classes: 11.30am – 12.30pm
Key Stage 1 & 2: 12.00pm - 1.00pm
The Trust’s catering company will provide a school lunch for all pupils which is funded through the Universal Infant Free School Meals (UIFSM) grant. Universal infant free school meals (UIFSM) provides funding for all government funded schools to offer free school meals to pupils in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2.
ASSEMBLIES / COLLECTIVE WORSHIP
These takes place throughout the week as a whole school and within each class. They include times of stories, prayers, songs, hymns, discussions and visitors. On Friday we will hold our weekly Alder Grove Celebration Assembly.
NURSERY
Pupils will attend Nursery either for the morning session: 8.30am - 11.30am or for the afternoon session 12.30pm – 3.30pm
Pupils will attend for both the morning and afternoon session.
Lunchtimes: 11.30am -12.30pm
Children will eat their pack lunch or can order a hot meal (additional cost) in the main hall under the supervision of the nursery staff and our lunchtime controllers.
Parents and carers of children who have been allocated a place for 30 hours per week will be offered the following options:
Parents/carers wishing to amend their child’s attendance pattern for the following term must notify the school via email before the start of the new term. If no communication is received, it will be assumed that the current arrangement will continue. Charges will apply for any additional hours requested, regardless of changes made to the funded hours. The cost of the additional hour is £6 each day.
BEFORE AND AFTER SCHOOL PROVISION
There is a Breakfast Club and After School Club available for Alder Grove CE Primary School for pupils from the age of 3 years old. This is run in house by the school.
Please see separate page on website for more details.
For more information, please email: wraparoundcare@aldergrove.wokingham.sch.uk

Parent/Carer Staff Association
Did you know that when you join our school, you are automatically enrolled in the Parent/Carer Staff Association?
The PCSA have been set up to raise extra funds for our school, so that we can buy fantastic resources to enhance the curriculum and wider school life.
We really appreciate the hard work that goes into running such events, but they are not possible without the help of YOU the parents/carers of our pupils. Perhaps you have a special skill, a fund raising idea, or contacts in the local area. You may even just have a spare half hour, to help with setting up an event or run a stall. All help is welcome and much appreciated.
To contact the PCSA please email: pcsa@aldergrove.wokingham.sch.uk

Uniform
RECEPTION, KEY STAGE 1 & KEY STAGE 2
Early Years Foundation Stage Uniform (Nursery & Reception)
Plain black trainers (similar style to school shoes – no large branding/range of colours) (generic)
Black jogging bottoms/leggings/shorts (generic)
School polo shirt*(branded & required)
School jumper/cardigan* (branded & required)
Black ankle socks (generic)
WINTER UNIFORM (KEY STAGE 1&2)
Black trousers/knee-length shorts
Black pinafore dress
Plain white shirt (no polo shirts)
School tie* (clip-on ties and elasticated ties available for KS1, full ties available for KS2)
Black school shoes (no ballet pump style shoes)
Jumper/cardigan with school logo*
Hair accessories should be navy or black: long hair tied back. No oversized hair accessories.
SUMMER UNIFORM (KEY STAGE 1&2)
Black trousers/knee-length shorts
Summer dress (pale purple and white gingham dress)
White ankle socks with summer dress
Plain white shirt (no polo shirts)
School tie* (clip-on ties and elasticated ties available for KS1, full ties available for KS2)
Black school shoes (no ballet pump style shoes)
Jumper/cardigan with school logo*
Hair accessories should be navy or black: long hair tied back. No oversized hair accessories.
PE KIT (KEY STAGE 1&2)
School polo shirt (EYFS & KS1) or school sports PE top (KS2)*
Black tracksuit trousers/leggings
School jumper/cardigan* (EYFS&KS1)
Black zip up hoody/jumper (KS2) - no large logos
OTHER
School book bag [branded or unbranded](EYFS/KS1)/
School Backpack (KS2 only - Year 3 to Year 5) - children can bring their own
Children will come to school in their PE kit on their PE days, therefore PE bags are not required.
*Available to purchase through our uniform suppliers. See below for details.
Our Approved Suppliers:
Smarter Impressions: Smarter Impressions Ordering Link
Goodies: Goodies Ordering Link
Summer uniform is typically worn from September to October half term and then again from the Easter holidays to the Summer holidays.
Winter uniform is typically worn from October half term until Easter holidays.
However, this is weather dependent and any changes will be communicated via the newsletter.
